newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar, Ifo data seen weighing on Frankfurt bourse.
newsitem.headline: Dollar, Ifo data seen weighing on Frankfurt bourse.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse was expected to move sideways or lower for the rest of the week as a weaker dollar weighed on German exporting stocks and data released on Wednesday dashed any hopes of a near-term rate cut.

"Before the Ifo and M3 data everything was looking really positive, but now there's a bit of inflation fear," said one Munich dealer. "Also the fact that the dollar has fallen below the 1.50 mark level is causing some people to take profit."
The IBIS DAX, measuring all-day electronic dealings in the 30 blue chip DAX index, was down 14.04 points at 2,767.50 points by 1604 GMT, below the bourse close of 2,774.50.
"The DAX could go sideways or be slightly weaker in the next couple of days," said one trader.

The respected German Ifo economics institute reported a sharp rise in business confidence in October, while the Bundesbank said M3 money supply growth stayed at 8.4 percent in October, well above its 1996 target of four to seven percent.

Although the day's most heavily traded stock was Deutsche Telekom, which has led volumes since shares in the telecommunications giant were first traded on Monday, volumes were subsiding and other stocks were moving into the spotlight.
Telekom was down 14 pfennigs at 31.86 marks in late IBIS.
Almost nine millon Telekom shares changed hands in computer IBIS dealings and over four million in bourse trade, significantly less than in the last two days.
Computer dealings have been temporarily extended by two hours to accomodate the additional volume.

The DAX's worst performer was industrial group Preussag AG, which fell over four percent after the company said profits for the business year that ended on September 30 fell sharply from the previous year.
Preussag shares were down almost six percent, or 22.20 marks to 354.20 marks in late IBIS dealings.
Amongst the medium capitalised stocks, SKW Trostberg, Merck and Continental were all higher after their respective nine month figures.
In late IBIS trade SKW was up 1.65 marks at 42.90 marks, Merck rose 1.50 marks to 56.60 marks and Continental gained 93 pfennigs to 26.62 marks.

Meanwhile, Metallgesellschaft resumed trade up 50 pfennigs at 28 marks, after the trade was suspended following the announcement of the sale of its banking operations. The company is due to report full year results on Friday.
